messages:
Ravi: FYI I hit a pyright regression in the Python SDK today. Autogen created list_tasks() typed as AsyncIterator[Optional[TaskModel]] in the .pyi stubs but the runtime never yields None. mypy ignores it but pyright makes callers add a bunch of `if x is None: continue` noise.

Nina: can you paste the minimal repro?

Ravi: sure: 
```py
# user code
async for t in client.list_tasks(workspace_id='w'):
    print(t.name)  # pyright: Object 't' could be None
```
Our generated factory uses Optional because the schema marks all fields nullable, and the model constructor helper returns Optional[TaskModel] in some branches. The pagination helper just flattens pages and never emits None.

Olivia: we've seen this pattern before. Two paths: tighten the .pyi to AsyncIterator[TaskModel] (better DX) or keep Optional and add stubs comments. Tightening seems fine if we can prove no None is yielded.

Ravi: I wrote a small audit script that runs against current generated clients—no generator yielded None. I'll open a PR to change the stub types and add a runtime assert in pagination.flatten_pages: `assert item is not None` to make the contract explicit.

Nina: instead of changing runtime, can we emit two overloads in the .pyi so callers get precise types for `raw_pages` flag? Example: 
```py
@overload
def list_tasks(..., *, raw_pages: Literal[False]) -> AsyncIterator[TaskModel]: ...
@overload
def list_tasks(..., *, raw_pages: Literal[True]) -> AsyncIterator[PageType]: ...
```
That helps callers who intentionally want raw page objects.

Olivia: love the overloads. Also consider generating a tiny compatibility .pyi shim for older SDK versions so we don't break downstream type-checking assumptions.

Ravi: good idea. For our CI: we only run mypy currently. I'm adding a pyright job to GH Actions that checks `stubs/` and sampleapps for pyright; that'll catch regressions early.

Nina: small nit: pyright is stricter about Optional. If we change the stubs we should also update the docs and release notes with a "Typing refinement" entry and link to migration snippet showing how to opt into raw pages if people relied on None semantics.

Olivia: is there any chance runtime yields None for partially-parsed items? Eg when the model factory returns None for invalid items during deserialization?

Ravi: current factory returns None only when the top-level object is missing. Pagination always iterates found items. But I'll add a test that simulates a broken parsed item to ensure pagination doesn't propagate None.

ci-bot: build queued: run-mypy, unit-tests, pyright-stubs (new).

Ravi: also proposing we update the codegen to avoid wrapping model types in Optional when it's for inner fields only. That reduces Optional propagation into the generator signature. It's a small codegen tweak.

Nina: sounds good. Can you add an entry in devex/autogen.md describing the invariant: "pagination yields only parsed items; None indicates missing page"? Would help future contributors.

Ravi: will do. Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/498 (WIP)

Olivia: assign to me for the .pyi review, Nina for CI changes.

Ravi: assigned. Thanks folks. :rocket:
